features.evidence: N4-R5 typed target、拒绝假成功动作层、有界分片 HTTP parser 与 durable MessageStore 已实现；core 将 MessageStore 装配进数值 account 的 Daemon/AccountActor，显式 projection 在 journal 与 ACK 之间落盘、恢复幂等重建，pipe 集成测试经 Daemon StoreReader 验证 OneBot get_msg 完整字段。普通 caligod 的 HTTP、HTTP POST、正向 WS、反向 WS 共用动作层；POST quick operation 结束后才扇出 WebSocket 事件。群 send 只有强 native 回执且匹配的持久 OneBot ID 可读时才返回成功。K3-D/K3-F 历史 receive 证据共包含 21 个不同的 UIN↔UID 对，样本内无冲突，其中仅一个联系人对有独立 profile UIN 交叉核对。固定版本 major.node 静态登记 `GroupService/getUidByUins(uinList)->uids` 与逆向方法 `getUinByUids`；已在两次用户授权的目标实例上启动 K4 owner-thread 只读样本：PID 48980 在 first_entry 后退出，无法判断 resolver API 是否到达；PID 48768 在组合式 QQNT session/GroupService 表面脚本期间变为无响应并退出。两次均无 resolver 结果，且无证据表明 API 已派发。修复了 bootstrap 将报告路径指向临时远程缓冲的生命周期缺陷，并将新探针分阶段；新 build 尚未现场验证。PID 48768 及后续新 root PID 8976 均已退出；PID 8976 的阶段日志止于 uid_map_binding_entered，结果文件为空，未证明 resolver API 派发。 Crashpad 三份 dump 现确认 PID 48980/48768/8976 均为 QQNT.dll+0x1F2AB8 读取 0x230 的 0xC0000005，三份栈均含 bridge 帧；PID8976 崩溃线程与 binding 阶段 owner TID 一致，但 resolver 未派发。无匹配 bridge PDB，且保存寄存器与紧邻 test/branch 不一致，根因未定；崩溃后没有重放。Crashpad 路径及脱敏摘要见事故台账与执行记录。报告路径生命周期缺陷已修复；探针继续细分为 no-op V8、状态初始化、linkedBinding、wrapper 读取。当前只见未选定的旧 root PID 47560，不得替代。新 build 尚待现场验证；通用私聊映射仍未建立，feat-006 保持 blocked。`getUserDetailInfoByUin` 返回掩码 UID；此前 `ProfileService/getUidByUin` 探针无可用响应。 固定构建 `wrapper.node` 静态断言 `ProfileService/getUidByUin` 与逆向方法各需 2 个 JavaScript 参数，`GroupService/getUidByUins`/`getUinByUids` 各需 1 个 JavaScript 列表参数；其 C++ callback RTTI 给出 UIN→UID 与 UID→UIN unordered-map 结果形状；ProfileService 第二参数语义未解析，三份 Crashpad dump 均定位到 V8 HandleScope 析构 AV；现有阶段记录未确认 resolver 派发或结果。Ghidra 定点反汇编支持清理路径定位但根因未闭合，通用映射未动态证明。HTTP→actor→fake bridge strong receipt→projection→get_msg 集成测试、慢头隔离及三类事件 transport 协议合同通过。真实 daemon_client projection 当前仍是 None；真实应用互通、通用私聊映射与 native receive/query 未验收，继续 blocked。 Turn 40: exact-build static metadata suggests ProfileService second argument is a caller/source string (`callFrom`; observed labels `node/BaseSearchAll` and `AvatarRenderer`); RTTI argument order is `(uint64_t,string)` forward and `(string,uint64_t)` reverse. N-API extraction and return encoding remain unconfirmed; the earlier one-argument probe was under-specified. HandleScope constructor/destructor ABI/layout matches current caller; null-isolate fail-closed guard and injected-symbol LAB tests pass 3/3, but do not reproduce the Crashpad register/branch inconsistency. No new mapping; R3/R4 remain open. 2026-11-07 UID-map V8 sanity prerequisite follow-up: exact-hash analysis ties the new pilot's HandleScope AV to the undersized TryCatch backing store, and the source correction plus isolated research release build are recorded in the execution ledger. The corrected bridge has no QQ runtime result; no resolver dispatch/result or UID mapping was observed, so feat-006 remains blocked. 2026-11-07 source audit confirms the callback response UID is diagnostic-only and current CPB receive events fail closed without mapped native_id and resolved sender_uin. No stable send/receive identity join was found; feature remains blocked. 2026-11-07 surface-only pilot on designated PID 31156 confirmed GroupService missing with api_call_attempted=false and no resolver stages. No UID result or response UID-to-CPB/native-ID relation was observed; remain blocked. 2026-11-13 SnowCat fixed-build evidence supplies the ProfileService call shape. The Caligo research CLI now has a 9.9.36-53644 hash-bound read-only mode with offline exact-key round-trip and rejection coverage. Caligo field validation and the response UID-to-CPB/native-ID join remain open. 2026-11-13 GroupMembers scoped snapshot and shared member-list/member-info routes have offline wrapper/real-pipe evidence; rich profile fetch and QQ field acceptance remain open. 2026-11-14 dual-account QQ probe reached owner bootstrap and clean shutdown in both instances; the reacquired wrapper returned profile_service_missing and dispatched neither resolver. The research probe now selects nt_1 from the exact-hash loaded wrapper module, with offline fixture coverage. Field retest on one restarted QQ root obtained ProfileService through nt_1, matched the exact UIN-to-UID-to-UIN round trip, and closed the owner pump cleanly. A subsequent no-UIN research probe obtained UIN and UID from the nt_1 ProfileService self-status notification on one fresh QQ root and matched both against independent evidence. A later fresh-root research probe verified the exact current-profile nickname and recorded the wrapper session ID with the host process nonce. Normal OneBot get_login_info returned the independently verified account and nickname through the exact-hash QQ 9.9.36-53644 owner and authenticated named pipe on one restarted root. Offline real-pipe regression covers revocation of an in-flight query and rejection of its stale epoch. Live account switching, reconnect and dual-account query isolation remain open. 2026-11-14 authorized continuation preflight found both existing QQ roots responsive with prior bridge builds still mapped and no running caligod/manager; both module audits rejected reattachment. Await fresh logged-in process generations before the dual-account query test; no new host API call or message submission occurred. After the user restarted both QQ instances, normal daemon/IPC LoginInfo queries on fresh A/B roots using the same pinned release matched independent QQ account/nickname evidence. Each endpoint rejected the other token with HTTP 403 and no token with 401; B still returned the same identity after A daemon/owner shutdown. Both daemon/owner pairs closed normally, both HTTP listeners closed, and both QQ roots remained responsive with bridges retained. This sequential-query sample does not cover account switching, reconnect, simultaneous in-flight replies, event/journal isolation or long-term quiescence. A separate research-only current-profile refresh probe now verifies host identity before one server-source fetch, joins the per-request Promise source/detail Map with a matching notification, and refuses timeout/drift or unverified listener cleanup. Exact-hash native static evidence and 22 synthetic scenarios exist; this is not a public get_stranger_info capability or QQ field acceptance. 2026-11-14 follow-up field evidence on a user-restarted A root returned profile_refresh_match for one current-self KSERVER request: per-request Promise source/detail and matching UID notification agreed with the independently checked QQ identity/nickname; listener removal returned, owner shutdown succeeded, and both QQ roots remained responsive. No message was sent. Public profile actions, other targets/fields, reconnect/account switch and long-term callback quiescence remain unverified. The subsequent self-only SelfProfile path is wired to get_login_info(no_cache=true), with distinct typed responses, no LoginInfo fallback, scoped owner cancellation and late-callback isolation. Final default/research workspace tests and isolated release build pass; a subsequent fresh A process passed one authenticated normal-entry get_login_info(no_cache=true) field sample on the exact pilot, with user_id/nickname matching an independent QQ card. The daemon and owner shut down, HTTP closed and both QQ roots remained responsive; DLLs remain mapped. Other targets/fields, real account switch/reconnect and long-term callback quiescence remain unverified, so blocked status is unchanged. A subsequent offline revocation audit passed 42 existing regressions and documented separate IPC/core/QQ identity lifetimes. A subsequent deterministic LAB reproduced old-query resumption and duplicate Disconnected results across same-scope rebind. Resident revocation now irreversibly marks pending queries, reports once and cancels on the owner; five new regressions and final default/research workspace tests pass. Real core-restart recovery and continuous QQ identity loss to global revocation remain open; no new field result or release was produced. On 2026-11-14 after the pinned wrapper text normalization fix, live B-to-A private and designated-group text reached SSE and the durable message store, and authenticated HTTP get_msg returned the same OneBot ID and message fields in both scenarios. A subsequent authenticated OneBot HTTP A-to-B private send returned success, the same persisted message ID was readable through get_msg, and the user observed one message on B. The designated-group OneBot HTTP sample also succeeded, matched sender get_msg and the persisted group identity, and became visible on A and B after B initially did not see it. Other transports and recovery criteria remain pending.
